name: Motor-generator set
summary: A motor mechanically coupled to a generator, used to isolate, change frequency or convert between AC and DC.
description: A motor-generator set is an electric motor driving a generator on a common shaft. It provides complete electrical isolation, conversion of frequency or voltage, or AC to DC conversion, and its rotating mass rides through short disturbances. Some sets add a flywheel or an engine on the same shaft for backup.

Drawings show two machine circles, one marked M and one marked G, joined by a mechanical coupling line. The motor input and generator output are on separate circuits, each with its own protection and earthing.

Efficiency is lower than a static converter and the rotating machines need maintenance, so motor-generator sets are now mainly found in legacy, test or special-purpose installations. The symbol does not show speed, coupling arrangement or ride-through time.
readingNotes: The coupling line shows a mechanical link, not an electrical one.
Earthing of the generator output is independent of the motor supply.
drawingChecklist: Reference flywheel or engine if fitted.
distinction: A motor-generator set converts through rotating machines; a static frequency converter uses power electronics.
